proposals.evidence: CDIAL 43 akṣi explicitly gives Phal. ac̣hi, Bengali ā̃khi, Hindi ā̃kh and Nepali ā̃kho “eye”. The survey affricate/nasal/kh variants identify this eye family; contracted ā̃kā retains a phonetic qualification. Reviewed comparator: Buksa aŋkʰ “eye” (f_63qufc3sfw4de). Any uncertain transfer between Indo-Aryan languages remains open under the user’s preference; source phonetic details are preserved.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 4147 distinguishes *gāvā (section 2), with Kalasha gak, Savi gāu and northern gāv, from gāvī (section 3), with Hindi gāī and Bshk. gay. Northern bare gā/gāu cannot simply be copied to gāvī without paradigm evidence. Reviewed comparator: Bshk gāī “cow” (f_a3okj55rinceg). Any uncertain transfer between Indo-Aryan languages remains open under the user’s preference; source phonetic details are preserved.
